name: Obadiah, who hid the prophets
charge: Taking an hundred prophets and hiding them by fifty in a cave, and feeding them with bread and water, while governor of Ahab’s house
summary: Obadiah was governor of Ahab’s house and feared the Lord greatly; when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the Lord, he took a hundred of them, hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water through a severe famine (1 Kings 18:3-4). Sent out by Ahab to search for grass, he met Elijah on the road and was afraid to carry his message, lest the Spirit carry the prophet away and Ahab kill him; Elijah swore he would show himself that day, and Obadiah went (1 Kings 18:5-16). His errand brought Ahab to Elijah and set the stage for Carmel (1 Kings 18:17-19).
offenseFull: In the third year of the drought the word came to Elijah to show himself to Ahab, and there was a severe famine in Samaria. Ahab called Obadiah, the governor of his house; and Obadiah feared the Lord greatly, for when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the Lord, he took a hundred prophets, hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water (1 Kings 18:1-4). The study notes say he put his own life in danger to save them. He was the ruler of the house of the very king whose wife was killing them. Cutting off the prophets, the teaching says, is not cutting someone off in their speech; she killed them, and a faithful man had to hide them. The Systemic Starvation class sets him among the righteous men of the famines, like Joseph in Egypt: in a time when rain meant everything, a man who feared the Lord greatly did not sit on his hands but kept something alive.

The famine was so sore it was hitting the animals, and Ahab sent Obadiah through the land to every fountain and brook to find grass to save the horses and mules, the two of them dividing the land between them (1 Kings 18:5-6). That was the fruit of the drought Elijah had pronounced. On the road Elijah met him; Obadiah knew him, fell on his face, and asked

whether he was his lord Elijah, and Elijah told him to go and tell his master that Elijah was there (1 Kings 18:7-8). Obadiah was afraid. Ahab had searched every nation and kingdom for Elijah and made them swear they had not found him; that is how badly Jezebel wanted him dead. If Obadiah went and the Spirit of the Lord carried Elijah off, Ahab would kill him for a false report. So he pleaded his own record: he had feared the Lord from his youth, and had hidden a hundred of the Lord’s prophets by fifty in a cave and fed them (1 Kings 18:9-14). Walking in Elijah’s Footsteps hears him saying, you are putting my life in danger, for Elijah was always here today and gone tomorrow. Elijah swore by the Lord of hosts that he would surely show himself to Ahab that day, and Obadiah went and told Ahab, and Ahab came to meet Elijah (1 Kings 18:15-16).
judgmentFull: A hundred prophets of the Lord lived through Jezebel’s killing and the famine because one man inside Ahab’s house feared the Lord. The class of 2026-07-18 draws out what she was really after: she was not trying merely to destroy one prophet; she was trying to stop the whole prophetic voice out of Israel, the whole movement, as the enemies of the congregation do today when they speak against one person, for the scripture says to smite the shepherd and the sheep will scatter (Zechariah 13:7). His errand then brought the king face to face with Elijah, and from that meeting came the gathering of all Israel to Carmel with the eight hundred and fifty prophets who ate at Jezebel’s table (1 Kings 18:17-19).

When Elijah later sat under the juniper tree and said he alone was left, the Lord answered that He had left Himself seven thousand in Israel whose knees had not bowed to Baal (1 Kings 19:10; 1 Kings 19:18). Walking in Elijah’s Footsteps notes that in his panic Elijah had forgotten what Obadiah told him about the hundred prophets he had hidden; he was not alone, and neither are the faithful today, for there are many out there waiting to call on the name of the Lord.

text.text: And Ahab called Obadiah, which was the governor of his house. (Now Obadiah feared the Lord greatly:
For it was so, when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the Lord, that Obadiah took an hundred prophets, and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water.)
And Ahab said unto Obadiah, Go into the land, unto all fountains of water, and unto all brooks: peradventure we may find grass to save the horses and mules alive, that we lose not all the beasts.
So they divided the land between them to pass throughout it: Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.
And as Obadiah was in the way, behold, Elijah met him: and he knew him, and fell on his face, and said, Art thou that my lord Elijah?
And he answered him, I am: go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah is here.
And he said, What have I sinned, that thou wouldest deliver thy servant into the hand of Ahab, to slay me?

As the Lord thy God liveth, there is no nation or kingdom, whither my lord hath not sent to seek thee: and when they said, He is not there; he took an oath of the kingdom and nation, that they found thee not.
And now thou sayest, Go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah is here.

And it shall come to pass, as soon as I am gone from thee, that the Spirit of the Lord shall carry thee whither I know not; and so when I come and tell Ahab, and he cannot find thee, he shall slay me: but I thy servant fear the Lord from my youth.
Was it not told my lord what I did when Jezebel slew the prophets of the Lord, how I hid an hundred men of the Lord’s prophets by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water?
And now thou sayest, Go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah is here: and he shall slay me.
And Elijah said, As the Lord of hosts liveth, before whom I stand, I will surely shew myself unto him to day.
So Obadiah went to meet Ahab, and told him: and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, Art thou he that troubleth Israel?
And he answered, I have not troubled Israel; but thou, and thy father’s house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the Lord, and thou hast followed Baalim.
Now therefore send, and gather to me all Israel unto mount Carmel, and the prophets of Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the groves four hundred, which eat at Jezebel’s table.
And it came to pass after many days, that the word of the Lord came to Elijah in the third year, saying, Go, shew thyself unto Ahab; and I will send rain upon the earth.
And Elijah went to shew himself unto Ahab. And there was a sore famine in Samaria.
